Author links open overlay panel, , , ,. While existing studies have largely focused on platform adoption and interactions with specific digital services, limited attention has been given to the dynamic nature of these platforms and how MSMEs strategically respond to such changes to improve their performance. To address this gap and draw on the Resource-Based View (RBV) and Dynamic Capability Theory (DCT), the present study investigates the mediating roles of innovation capabilities and digital IT capabilities in the relationship between business strategy and MSME performance. Practically, it underscores the importance of developing technological adaptability to ensure the long-term sustainability of Indonesian MSMEs. Policymakers can further leverage these findings by designing targeted training programs and financial incentives that simultaneously build MSMEs' innovation competencies and digital capabilities, thereby strengthening their resilience and growth potential in an increasingly digital marketplace.
